newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES FOR ATLETICO V REAL MADRID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES FOR ATLETICO V REAL MADRID.

text.p: Facts and figures for Saturday's Spanish league match between Atletico Madrid and Real Madrid at the Vicente Calderon stadium.

Atletico Madrid: Founded in April 1903 as Athletic de Madrid, a name kept until the Spanish Civil War when the club joined forces with Madrid's Club Aviacion. Victorious fascist dictator Francisco Franco forbade the use of anglicised names such as Athletic and Sporting, and the club became known as Atletico Aviacion from 1939 until finally changing its name to Atletico de Madrid in 1946. In English this is generally shortened to Atletico Madrid.
Ground: Vicente Calderon stadium (named after former club president), capacity 56,000.
Manager: Radomir Antic (Serbia)
Record league appearances: Abelardo, 399 games.
Real Madrid: Founded in 1902.
Ground: Santiago Bernabeu stadium (named after former club president), capacity 106,000.
Manager: Fabio Capello (Italy).
Record appearances: Carlos Santillana, 461.
Past matches between Atletico and Real:
At Vicente Calderon: Played 61, Atletico won 22, Real won 22, 17 draws.
At Santiago Bernabeu: Played 61, Real won 43, Atletico won 11, seven draws.
Total: Played 122, Atletico won 33, Real won 65, 24 draws.
Corresponding fixture in last five seasons (Atletico first, starting 1991-92): 2-0, 1-1, 0-0, 0-2, 1-2.
Fascinating Facts:

-- Both Atletico and Real were founding members of the Spanish first division in 1928-29. Together with Athletic Bilbao and Barcelona, Real have never been relegated. Atletico have only spent four seasons in the second division but have twice avoided relegation in curious circumstances. They should have gone down in 1934 but were saved by a decision to increase the first division from 10 to 12 teams. Two years later they were again close to relegation when the 1936-39 Spanish Civil War intervened. When the league restarted in 1939 Oviedo withdrew because their ground had been used as a prison camp. Atletico won a play-off to remain in the first division and went on to take the next two l

-- The prefix 'Real', meaing royal, is held by another 10 first division clubs. The Real Madrid club shield incorporates a crown to reflect its royal patronage. The club play in an all-white strip and their fans are sometimes called 'merengues' (meringues) as a result.
-- Atletico are known as the 'colchoneros' from the Spanish word 'colchon' meaning mattress. Earlier this century mattresses made in Spain were predominantly red and white, Atletico's club colours.

-- Atletico have recently resuscitated the colours of their first-ever team strip, light blue and white, as a second change for away games. There was outrage amongst Atletico old-timers when the team took the field in the Champions' League game at Steaua Bucharest wearing white instead of the traditional dark blue shorts.

-- Real Madrid's basketball side has been just as successful in the European Cup as the football outfit, but the club no longer competes in other sports. Atletico's basketball and handball teams were recently disbanded by club owner Jesus Gil in a controversial cost-cutting measure.

-- Although few people would dispute that Argentine striker Alfredo di Stefano was Real's greatest-ever player, he may not be the most famous. Latin singing idol Julio Iglesias was once a goalkeeper for one of the club's reserve teams, and only took up music because of an injury. Like 1980's Mexican striker Hugo Sanchez, di Stefano was close to signing for both Barcelona and Atletico.
-- The reserve teams of both Real and Atletico play in the Spanish second division, but would only be promoted if the first teams were relegated. Atletico reserves recently beat Real 3-0.
